topic.title: Stochastic Sampling and Langevin Dynamics
topic.overview: Sampling algorithms approximate probability distributions by constructing a sequence of random updates. This topic studies how stochastic gradients, proximal steps, variance reduction, and interacting particles can make that process scalable. Its central challenge is controlling the difference between the distribution an algorithm produces and the target distribution it is meant to represent.
topic.whyItMatters: Cheap updates do not guarantee cheap accurate samples: noise, discretization, dimension, and dependence between samples all matter. Convergence analyses make these trade-offs explicit, while experiments test whether the assumptions and predicted improvements remain useful on concrete inference or optimization tasks.
topic.evolution: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics in 2011 combines mini-batch updates with injected noise and annealed step sizes. Later work examines geometry, splitting methods, and nonasymptotic bounds. A 2024 stochastic proximal sampler addresses non-log-concave targets; 2026 mean-field work reduces particle-interaction costs using a selected coreset while retaining conditional convergence guarantees.
openQuestions: Which theoretical error measures best predict the usefulness of downstream posterior estimates?
How can sampling methods remain efficient when the target has widely separated modes?

papers.tldr: Mirror mean-field Langevin dynamics extends distribution optimization to convex constrained domains with convergence and particle-approximation guarantees.

papers.title: On the Robustness of Langevin Dynamics to Score Function Error
papers.tldr: Arbitrarily small score-estimation error can still leave Langevin sampling far from its target throughout polynomial time horizons.

papers.title: Robust Stochastic Gradient Posterior Sampling with Lattice Based Discretisation
papers.tldr: SGLRW changes the covariance structure of stochastic-gradient sampling to improve robustness while retaining asymptotic correctness.

papers.title: Thinned Mean Field Langevin Dynamics
papers.tldr: Kernel thinning reduces mean-field Langevin interaction costs from quadratic to N to the three-halves while retaining comparable convergence guarantees under mild conditions.

papers.title: Variational inference via Gaussian interacting particles in the Bures-Wasserstein geometry
papers.tldr: A gradient-free population of interacting Gaussian particles offers an effective variational-inference optimizer for the tested low-dimensional, non-log-concave targets.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Non-Log-Concave Sampling with Variance Reduction and Applications to Inverse Problems
papers.tldr: A variance-reduced gradient-free Langevin sampler gains finite-run convergence guarantees and supports posterior sampling for black-box inverse problems.
